checks_run.procedure: Steps 2 and 3. Does an engine code-generation path that the tests DO exercise fail them, at validation and at evaluation time? Probe the static class again: new key forms Q1–Q5, and the allowlisted ../value.ts (V1, V2).
checks_run.command: node probes/guard-layers-probe.mjs $TMPDIR/review-p3b (forms Q1–Q5, V1, V2, S1–S3); node probes/exercised-probe.mjs $TMPDIR/review-p3 and $TMPDIR/review-p3b

checks_run.expected: any exercised code-generating path fails unit-formula-nocodegen (ADR-0024 §6 layer-3 guarantee); vm/inspector cannot be reached through an allowlisted import (§6 'Layers 1–2 refuse those')
checks_run.actual:
FAIL. Both ADR statements are contradicted.

Q1–Q5 pass lint and the scan, and each is refused at run time (20 flag-only failures). These are the residual §6 states honestly: a key assembled from values no static rule sees, on an ordinary function variable.

S2: evaluation-time code generation when a value has a trailing fraction zero. It is refused at run time (6 flag-only failures), because formula.test.ts asserts exact values there.

S1: tokenize.ts describe() generates code for U+00C0–U+1FFF. lint 0, scan 0, unit-formula-nocodegen 0 (190/190), control 0.

S3: evaluation-time code generation when m = '50' (the fuzz VARS). Same result: all three layers pass.

exercised-probe.log, and the clean rerun, prove these paths RUN under the flag:
- validateFormula('été') → 'Syntax error at offset 0: the formula could not be processed (EvalError)', with params.reason 'internal';
- fuzz.test.ts's own seeded 10,000 byte strings hit the EvalError 2,805 times, and its 20,000 grammar strings hit S3's path 41 times;
- every one is swallowed as formula.syntax, and the tests pass (57/57, exit 0).

Cause:
- index.ts validateFormula and evaluateFormula catch every error as internalProblem (formula.syntax, offset 0).
- fuzz.test.ts checkOutcome and the payload test accept formula.syntax.
- formula.test.ts's offset-0 rejected rows accept it too.

V1: `import { runInThisContext } from "node:vm"` in packages/shared/src/value.ts, called in checkDecimal. lint 0, scan 0, unit-formula-nocodegen 0, control 0, so it passes all three layers.
- ../value.ts is allowlisted, but no formula rule covers it (diff-scan S1e: no-eval, no-new-func, no-implied-eval, no-restricted-imports and no-restricted-globals are unset).
- The scan reads only formula/*.ts.
- V2 (new Function in value.ts) is refused only at run time (59 flag-only failures).

The shipped value.ts is clean (S1d: only a class constructor) and unchanged in P3 (S1c). This is a guard gap, not an exploit. It keeps F-DG3-100 open (Low, non-mandatory; see the verifications sidecar).

checks_run.expected: every statement exactly true
checks_run.actual:
Mostly true, but two statements are false, so the result is FAIL.

True:
- Layers 1 and 2 contain what is listed (SEC-R3-14, lint.log, diff-scan S1f: the engine sources get the allowlist and 13 restricted globals).
- The canary asserts what is described, and the guard cannot be silently lost (SEC-R3-15).

(a) 'Guarantee. Any engine path that generates code from a string fails the engine's tests, provided a test exercises it.' S1 and S3 are exercised and do not fail (SEC-R3-16).
(b) 'Not covered by the flag … Layers 1–2 refuse those, through the import allowlist and the process ban.' V1 reaches node:vm through the allowlisted ../value.ts, and no layer refuses it.

The residual paragraph names only unexercised paths, and does not mention ../value.ts being outside every formula rule.

What the repair closes:

Why F-DG3-100 stays open: two reproducible paths pass all three layers, and each contradicts ADR-0024 §6.
(1) The run-time 'guarantee' fails for exercised paths. validateFormula and evaluateFormula catch the EvalError as formula.syntax/'internal', and fuzz.test.ts and the offset-0 table accept that. A code-generating path in tokenize.ts was hit 2,805 times by the fuzz's own seeded inputs under the flag, and one at evaluation time 41 times, and every test passed.
(2) The import allowlist admits ../value.ts, which no formula rule covers. node:vm imported there and called from checkDecimal passes lint, the scan and the run-time layer.
The shipped engine and value.ts contain no dynamic code, so this is a guard gap, not an exploit.
